thread:
claire: Heads-up — I noticed the 429 example under docs/error-reference/429-behavior.md still recommends immediate retries without honoring server hints. That could cause cascading failures.

omar: which example specifically?

claire: the "simple retry" block under "examples". It retries in a tight loop. We should show: 1) prefer Retry-After if present, 2) prefer server-sent X-RW-Backoff if present, 3) else exponential backoff with jitter, and 4) a context-eviction fallback (drop oldest non-essential turns) before retrying.

rachel: +1. I'll prepare a compact set: a tiny curl dev-check (annotated brittle), a Node SDK pattern, and a Python snippet that demonstrates circuit-breaker after N attempts. Keep snippets minimal so maintainers can mirror them across SDKs.

claire: also add a short migration note for docs maintainers: update docs/sdk-snippets/{python,js,go}/429_* to keep parity and pin snippet versions in the PR description.

omar: please include a QA repro script (dev sandbox) and a one-paragraph "how we validated" so QA can sign off quickly.

rachel: draft ready, pushing a PR shortly. curl snippet I plan to use (with warning):

```
# dev-only brittle header probe
RA=$(curl -sI -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.com/v1/respond | sed -n 's/.*Retry-After: \([^\)]*\)/\1/ip')
[ -n "$RA" ] && sleep ${RA%\r}
```

omar: nice. For SDK snippets show normalization: min 1s for RA <1, add +/-25% jitter, cap retries to 5, then trip circuit-breaker and escalate.

claire: include streaming guidance: when a stream is cut with 429, use resumable tokens if available, else reconnect with backoff and only resend delta prompts. Don't recommend blind full replays.

rachel: opening PR now -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1101 Labels: docs, 429-playbook, needs-approval. Requesting reviews from @claire and @omar.
